source_tamil_lines: கீசகன் ஆசை கொண்ட கிச்சிலிப் பழமடி நீ...
காச நோய்போல வந்த காதலுக்கு மருந்தடி நீ...
english_lines: You are the kichili fruit that Kichaka desired, di...
You are the medicine, di, for love that came like consumption...
notes: The unusual printed forms `வைபோக`, `சைபோக`, and `சைரந்திரியே` are carried into English by transliteration rather than normalized to a familiar dramatic text.
`கிச்சிலிப் பழம்` remains `kichili fruit`, preserving the specific comic fruit image.
`காச நோய்` is rendered as `consumption`, retaining the disease-love comparison rather than softening it to lovesickness.

english_lines: O handsome one, Mammudha, desire-struck Kichaka!
notes: The verified Tamil prints `மம்முதா`; the English retains it as `Mammudha` rather than silently correcting it to a familiar mythological name.

english_lines: You came in madness, twirling your moustache,
You monkey! You great big monkey!
notes: `டேய்` is retained as `Dei` because its taunting spoken force would be lost in a polite English address.
The monkey insult and moustache-twirling mockery are kept direct.
The repeated `வாலாட்டமா...?` taunt is retained exactly as repetition, keeping the animal/mock-heroic image.

translator_notes: The translation keeps the song as a noisy village performance full of interjections, taunts, Mahabharata references, disease imagery, fruit imagery and deliberately coarse ridicule.
Source-anomalous printed forms remain visible through transliteration; translation is not used to repair the Tamil witness.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
